important_information: Documented Inspector recording adds runtime cost, particularly for array modifications; disable after debugging for releases.
Waitless action bursts can exhaust a tick's workload; yield or batch when simultaneous completion is unnecessary, rather than treating all finite loops as equally unsafe.
Rule conditions are documented as ordered and short-circuiting; put cheap/selective gating before expensive array/spatial calculations. Article recommends less frequently changing conditions early.
Player hero/slot filters reduce evaluation scope, but changing away from that hero/slot immediately aborts an active rule; optimization changes lifecycle behavior.

Startup load can be reduced by delaying initialization until spawn, gating expensive conditions, consolidating selected rules, and staggering player initialization with Wait(Slot Of(Event Player)*0.016).

Sparse evaluation moves expensive conditions into an If inside a waited loop; example polls at 0.2 seconds instead of 0.016, trading reaction precision for cost. It can miss timing-sensitive behavior and is not interchangeable with per-tick event checks.

Disabled rules/actions/conditions and empty rules reportedly do not consume execution cost, although empty rules still appear in Inspector. This differs from element counting, where disabling does not reclaim elements.

Mutating any array element reportedly causes every rule condition referencing that variable to be reconsidered, even if they reference a different index; monolithic state arrays can amplify invalidation.

Damage-event rules cannot rerun for the same active context while waiting; a Wait used as throttling can discard needed triggers. Dealt Damage is per attacker, so simultaneous multi-target damage can process only one victim; Took Damage is per victim and allows one active instance for each victim.
High-frequency SMG/DOT/beam damage events can dominate load; any wait-based reduction must explicitly consider which event information will be lost.
Built-in Mapped/Filtered/Sorted Array operations are documented as often cheaper than manual For Global Variable loops; multidimensional array processing is expensive.
